newsitem.title: SPAIN: SOCCER-INTERMEDIARY IMPROVES RONALDO OFFER, SAY BARCELONA.
newsitem.headline: SOCCER-INTERMEDIARY IMPROVES RONALDO OFFER, SAY BARCELONA.

text.p: Barcelona have been offered an extra billion pesetas ($6.9 million) by an unnamed intermediary to push through the transfer of striker Ronaldo to Inter Milan, the president of the Spanish club said on Friday.
Jose Luis Nunez restated his belief that Ronaldo was still a Barcelona player, and said the Brazilian would be asked to make the pre-season tour of Sweden later in the month.
The four billion pesetas ($27.6 million) theoretically needed to make Ronaldo a free agent was paid last month.
Barcelona have refused to recognise the transfer, citing a FIFA directive that only Spanish clubs are entitled to pay the 'withdrawal clause' used in players' contracts in the country.
Overseas sides are instead obliged to negotiate with the clubs of players based in Spain.
Nunez said Ronaldo, who is currently in Brazil, would be asked to return on July 21 for the Swedish tour.
In other news Nunez announced that he would sign a multi-million dollar new contract later on Friday with an unnamed sportswear firm.
Commentators say Nike edged out current suppliers Kappa in the bidding for the lucrative contract.

Nunez said Barcelona would be paid 1.6 billion pesetas ($11 million) a year, and that cash advances and other aspects of the deal would make the contract around 21 billion pesetas ($145 million) over 10 years.
The contract starts at the end of the 1997-98 season and includes a clause to pay two years' interest payments on $18 million to be used to sign a new player.
Firenze's Gabriel Batistuta and Monaco's Sonny Anderson head the running as the most likely signings.
The sportswear company will also open a 5,000 square metre shop inside the Camp Nou stadium, while Barcelona will take an undisclosed percentage of profits on sales of club kit in all locations.
The deal came at the end of another good season for the finances of the Catalan side.

Nunez announced gross profits of over two billion pesetas ($13.8 million) for the season just ended. The payment of Ronaldo's 'withdrawal clause' had not been included in the accounts, because technically it should be valued after the end of the season.
TV income had more than tripled in the past season, to 4,860 million pesetas ($33.5 million), said Nunez.
The club has budgeted over 12 billion pesetas ($82.7 million) for next season, 25 per cent more than for the season just ended, he said.
